$comment: SHARED SMS PARSING CONTRACT — read by BOTH the .NET and Android test suites.
The two parsers cannot share code (C# and Kotlin), so this corpus is the mechanism that
keeps them from diverging. Every fixture states the expected outcome once; both suites
assert against it. A change on one platform that is not matched on the other fails there.
This file exists because the platforms HAD already diverged: Android required a provider
reference before auto-posting while the server did not, so a message truncated from
'Cash In of GHS 500.00 ... Ref: ...' to 'Cash In of GHS 5' was held on Android and posted
All MSISDNs, references and names are synthetic. No real customer data belongs here:
fixtures are committed, searchable, and copied into bug reports.
autoPostAllowed is the safety-critical field. When false, the platform must preserve the
evidence for review and must NOT create a financial transaction or move any balance.

fingerprintCases.note: Baseline for the shared fingerprint algorithm.
Same event; MSISDN written internationally. Must fingerprint identically.
Trailing zeros must not change identity.
Providers report seconds inconsistently; truncation to the minute absorbs it.
A different minute is a different event.
A cash-in and a cash-out of the same value are opposite events.
